I farm only 3.0 mu, so every bag of fertilizer and every irrigation matters. I will start from what has worked around Quzhou and only push a little where I think the return is real. For the wheat-maize land, I will keep most of the area in the usual rotation because that is the steady money and I have well water, so I can hold yield better than dryland fields. I will put 2.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize, and I will leave 1.0 mu for cotton. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard on grain, because if wheat or maize loses stand or ear size, that loss is bigger than saving a few dozen yuan. So on wheat I will use a bit fuller base, then chase with nitrogen at jointing; on maize I will feed enough for a solid ear but not go crazy on phosphorus because the wheat season already leaves some effect in the soil; on cotton I will not starve potassium because if bolls are weak, the whole field looks empty. Since some family labor is away working, I will also keep the operations simple: rotary tillage for wheat, no-tillage or direct seeding for summer maize if the stubble condition allows, and ordinary spring tillage for cotton. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen neighbors get stable yield, because I trust what I can see in nearby fields more than talk.
